transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-27 10:00 PT / 18:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miller (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Peregrine Head of ML), Lena Ortiz (Infra Lead), Marcus Chen (CTO)

Summary:
Quick sync to review this week's POC bench results comparing Redwood runtime to their incumbent provider, triage a latency spike observed at 95th percentile, discuss routing and quantization tradeoffs, and agree next steps for a short stress run and sample workload upload.

Topics:
- Bench numbers: p50/p95 throughput comparisons vs baseline
- Observed variance during bursts and cold-starts
- Routing fallback policy and dedicated slot request
- Quantization effect on quality vs latency
- Next steps and responsibilities

Action items (recorded in notes above)

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan Miller: Okay great, uh thanks everybody for joining. We have about 45, 50 minutes, we'll try to be respectful. Quick roll call—Priya are you with me?
00:07 Priya Desai: Yep I'm here. Hey Samir, Lena, Marcus, thanks for the time.
00:11 Samir Patel: Hey, thanks Jordan. Sorry ran late ramping up the cluster.
00:15 Lena Ortiz: Sorry yeah, had a quick infra change earlier, all good now.
00:18 Jordan Miller: Cool. Quick agenda—Priya will walk through the bench results we ran Wednesday, then we'll triage that 95th percentile spike you flagged, routing decisions, and then next steps. Sound okay?
00:28 Marcus Chen: Yep that's fine.
00:30 Priya Desai: All right, I'm sharing screen now — I posted the numbers in the sheet but I'll speak through high level. So baseline here is your incumbent cloud endpoint, labeled "IncumbentCloud" in the sheet. We ran identical prompt sets, same sequence length distribution and sampling settings. Key numbers: Redwood runtime with prefix KV caching on and batching window at 6ms gave p50 token latency of ~8.1ms per token and p95 of 32.5ms. Incumbent was p50 about 12.3ms and p95 about 58ms in our run. So fairly healthy delta, especially at p95.
01:08 Samir Patel: Okay, that's encouraging. But we saw in our overnight run some 95 spikes up to 120ms for a small subset—was that in your run?
01:17 Priya Desai: We did see a bump in one of the burst patterns. The thing to note is that the spikes correlated with concurrent KV cache misses when many requests used different prefixes, so the effective per-request cache hit rate dropped. There's also some routing fallbacks—if the primary node for that shard was under pressure the router moved a portion to a compatible but smaller quantized instance which briefly increased latency.
01:42 Lena Ortiz: That matches what we saw. We have a workload that mixes conversational history and one-off queries so prefix reuse is not perfect. Would increasing the cache retention help?
01:53 Priya Desai: Yes, increasing retention window and also enabling a micro-batching window helps. We tested 6ms vs 12ms windows: 12ms reduces p95 on heavy burst by about 15-18% but increases p50 slightly because of batching delay. It's a latency vs throughput tradeoff.
02:12 Jordan Miller: Important to call out that for your SLA candidate (<= 50ms p95) we can hit it in our tests with a combination of retention tuning, slightly larger Dedicated slot, or routing policy that prefers nodes with warmer KV.
02:25 Marcus Chen: On Dedicated, what's the cost delta for reserving one extra slot for the pilot? I want a guardrail so customer traffic doesn't see fallback to lower-tier instances.
02:33 Jordan Miller: I'll send a formal pricing delta after this call; very roughly a single dedicated slot to meet your throughput is about a 22% uplift vs current pilot commit, plus optional burst capacity which is metered. I'll put that in the note.
02:44 Samir Patel: Cool. Can you explain the "compatible but smaller quantized instance"—we were worried quality might drop if requests get routed there.
02:53 Priya Desai: Sure. So in the routing policy we define compatibility by model family and quantization level. A smaller quantized instance might be int8 or q4_0 which is faster but can have slight token distribution shifts. In our evals we saw BLEU-style metric drift of about 0.6% on your generation prompt set with q4 at default, and no user-facing regressions for ~95% of prompts. But your domain has long-form technical outputs, so we should run targeted quality checks.
03:24 Lena Ortiz: Right that drift could matter for us. Do you have the exact prompts where drift happened?
03:28 Priya Desai: We flagged 24 prompts; I'll share a CSV with the examples and the diff metrics after. Some are rare temp code-gen artifacts.
03:36 Marcus Chen: Also curious about cold-starts — when nodes scale up, do you pre-warm KV cache? We saw initial 500ms tails on cold allocations earlier in the week.
03:46 Priya Desai: Good q. We do warm caches for pinned model variants when requested but autoscale new nodes will start cold. For pilot we can pre-allocate a small warm pool to eliminate that cold tail. That is typically part of a Dedicated slot plan.
03:58 Jordan Miller: To add, the warm pool is configurable and you can set a pre-warm concurrency or time window. It costs a bit but it's predictable.
04:06 Samir Patel: On batching—why did you choose a 6ms window initially?
04:09 Priya Desai: We started conservative because your p50 targets were tight; 6ms gets lower median while still collecting some batching benefits. When burstiness rose we experimented with 12ms which slightly raised p50 but tightened p95. It's workload dependent.
04:22 Lena Ortiz: One operational question — in your logs we saw a spike in CPU on the router during the fallback. Is that expected?
04:28 Priya Desai: There is a tiny overhead in routing decisions during heavy churn due to re-sharding/placement decisions. We can tune routing evaluation window to be less aggressive so it avoids moving requests mid-burst. That's one quick knob to flip for the short term.
04:41 Marcus Chen: What about security/compliance—if we move to Dedicated slot, does data residency change? We need to ensure no cross-tenant KV leakage.
04:50 Jordan Miller: For Dedicated we guarantee tenant isolation and the KV store is scoped per customer. We can walk through SOC2 artifacts and our VPC/private deployment options in the next call. I'll add that to next steps.
05:02 Samir Patel: Great. Back to the bench numbers — can you walk through the throughput numbers? We have to match about 1200 reqs/min during peak.
05:10 Priya Desai: On throughput, with the 6ms window and two dedicated slots in our lab config we hit ~1400 reqs/min with stable p95 below 50ms. With single slot and burst enabled we sustained 1100–1250 reqs/min but saw occasional p95 breaching during the synthetic bursts. For comparison, Incumbent was around 1000 reqs/min with larger variance.
05:36 Lena Ortiz: The pattern we saw is mid-day burst is small but frequent. Suggest we prioritize reducing p95 over median slightly.
05:43 Priya Desai: Agreed. For that we recommend: 1) increase batching window to 10–12ms, 2) increase cache retention to keep more prefixes hot, 3) set routing policy to avoid cross-shard migration during 30s windows, 4) reserve one extra slot or configure burst autoscaling.
06:00 Jordan Miller: Quick question on quantization — if we pin model to non-quantized variant for high-quality outputs, how much throughput do we lose?
06:08 Priya Desai: Typically non-quantized fp16 gives best quality but could be 1.6x slower on token latency vs q4 variants on same hardware. So you trade CPU/GPU cycles. We often suggest mixed strategy: critical routes pinned to fp16, bulk text-only routes to quantized.
06:24 Samir Patel: Sounds reasonable. For our use-case we have 3 critical API routes and a bulk low-risk ingest. We can probably pin critical.
06:31 Marcus Chen: We also want to run a 95p stress test with a real sample workload. We can scrub PII and provide that. Timeline?
06:37 Jordan Miller: That would be ideal. If you can upload the trace by March 2 we'll run the sweep by March 3 and share results and full traces.
06:45 Lena Ortiz: Yep I'll get it in. We'll scrub and upload to the S3 share.
06:49 Priya Desai: We'll run both retention/batching permutations and routing toggle pass/fail tests and capture p50/p95/p99. Also we'll capture quality diffs for pinned vs quantized.
06:59 Samir Patel: One more question — are there any known regressions with function-calling or tool-integrations on quantized instances? We use tool calls in about 12% of requests.
07:09 Priya Desai: Function-calling payloads are generally unaffected, but quantization can change tokenization boundaries occasionally leading to slight parse differences; we haven't seen functional failures but we will include function-call tests in the next sweep.
07:21 Jordan Miller: Great. Any other blockers?
07:23 Marcus Chen: Not from my side. We need the formal pricing and the routing doc and the 24 prompt diffs.
07:29 Jordan Miller: We'll deliver those: pricing delta (Jordan), routing policy write-up (Priya), prompt diffs and CSV (Priya).
07:36 Samir Patel: And we'll provide the 5k request trace (Lena).
07:39 Lena Ortiz: Yep.
07:41 Priya Desai: One small note — we spotted a mislabel in the sheet where one of the tests was run with temperature 0.6 vs 0.2; explain the small throughput variance. I'll correct and re-run that test and post corrected numbers tonight.
07:52 Jordan Miller: Cool, appreciate the catch.
07:54 Samir Patel: Thanks—this has been productive. I want us to aim for the stress run early next week so we can decide on Dedicated slot by mid-week.
08:03 Jordan Miller: Sounds good. We'll get the artifacts out by Friday and run the stress on Tuesday if trace arrives Monday. Anything else before we wrap?
08:10 Marcus Chen: No, that's it for now.
08:12 Jordan Miller: All right thanks everyone. We'll follow up with notes and next steps.
08:16 (call ends)
